source_text: Ficus protulit grossos suos; vineae florentes dederunt odorem. Surge, amica mea, speciosa mea, et veni. Columba mea in foraminibus petrae, in caverna maceriae. Ostende mihi faciem tuam; sonet vox tua in auribus meis. Haec Libri Tertii prima series a cubili umbroso usque ad vocem turturis et foraminis petrae.
pass_a_gloss: Fig put-forth green-figs its; vines flowering gave smell. Arise, friend my, fair my, and come. Dove my in holes of-rock, in hollow of-wall...
pass_b_english: [[The fig tree has put forth its green figs; the flowering vines have given fragrance. Arise, my friend, my fair one, and come. My dove in the clefts of the rock, in the hollow of the wall. Show me your face; let your voice sound in my ears >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:13-14]]. This is the Third Book’s first series, from the shaded couch as far as the turtledove’s voice and the cleft of the rock.
